blocks.x: The engineering substrate, as deployed in current programs:

items: Unity Catalog As The Single Governance Plane
One place where every asset has an owner, a classification and a policy.
Delta Lake
Bronze-silver-gold layers with schema enforcement — the lakehouse done in the order that survives audits.
Lakehouse Federation Where Data Must Stay Put
Query where the data lives when policy forbids copying it — federation instead of duplication.
Mlflow
Every experiment and model version recorded — the difference between research and production.
Databricks Workflows As The Orchestration Spine
One scheduler for every pipeline and job — retries, lineage and failure alerts built in.
data contracts
Typed schemas with owners and freshness expectations, agreed before a pipeline is allowed to ship.
Delta / Iceberg tables
Open table formats underneath everything we build, so your data never belongs to a vendor.
streaming ingest
Events land in seconds, not overnight batches — the precondition for decisions that happen in the moment.
Unity Catalog governance
A single governance plane over tables, models and notebooks — access your auditors can replay.

blocks.x: Joint delivery on Databricks Alliance is designed for handover from the first week — runbooks written as we go, decisions mapped to your owners, nothing that only we can operate.
Artifacts, not anecdotes — at the first-quarter close your team holds:

items: Joint architecture pack
the adapted reference architecture, reviewed by the vendor's own field team before it reaches your architects
Certified delivery pod
engineers badged on both stacks, with the vendor escalation path printed inside the runbook
Support map
who calls whom at 3 a.m. — the joint escalation tree, tested in a joint exercise rather than assumed from a PDF

blocks.x: Ask for the Databricks reference pack — or bring your use case to a joint working session with both platform teams.
